title: Blackhawks signing veteran defenseman Ian Cole to 1-year deal: Source
content:
CHICAGO — You can add defenseman Ian Cole to the list of players who end up playing their 1,000th career NHL game with an unlikely team.

Cole, who is sitting on 990 career games, has agreed to a one-year contract with the Chicago Blackhawks on Wednesday, according to a league source who spoke under the condition of anonymity to address negotiations that aren’t public. Cole’s cap hit will be $4 million with the potential to make an additional $750,000 in bonuses. The Blackhawks will become the 10th team Cole has played for in his career.

Cole, who turned 37 in February, spent the last two seasons with the Utah Mammoth. He had three goals and 20 assists and averaged 18:16 of ice time last season.

Cole fills a need for the Blackhawks as an experienced defenseman who can play on the penalty kill. The Blackhawks’ six other defensemen are 25 years old or younger. Cole led the Mammoth in short-handed ice time last season. With the Blackhawks trading Connor Murphy at the deadline last season and Louis Crevier recently, they lost two of their top penalty-killing defensemen.

The question will be how Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill utilizes Cole with the six other defensemen who are expected to receive ice time next season. Cole joins fellow left-handed defensemen Bowen Byram, who signed a six-year extension Wednesday, Alex Vlasic and Kevin Korchinski, and right-handed defensemen Artyom Levshunov and Sam Rinzel.
